title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

sense.text:
The ungodly say “Let our strength be the law of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.” We’re the feeble. Their strength is the law: that is why they have their people in the law firms, and why they are funding senators to change things.

When you have money you can change the definitions of words and rewrite history, and they are doing it. Things that were never on Google are put up now that the Israelites are bringing the truth out, and an enemy of our people boasted that, thanks to Google, anyone who speaks against them will have it follow them for the rest of their life, on the job, even looking for a spouse. Bringing out facts, identifying the people correctly from the Bible, they call that an attack, terrorist speech, hate speech, and they use all these things to turn the tide against truth. So get snapshots and hard copies, because these people are wicked as hell.

The scriptures discuss two events where Israelites were set free from debt, from working the land, and from servitude: servitude, not slavery, and the word is used on purpose. The first is the seventh year of release, the year the land is released. “Six years thou shalt sow thy land”: work your land for six years.

“But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat.” When you have property you are to let your land rest and lie still in the seventh year, and what the poor leave, “the beasts of the field shall eat.” The same goes for the vineyard and the oliveyard.

“Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest.” The seventh-day sabbath goes for the land as well: just as man and beast rest on the seventh day, the land rests in the seventh year. That is the seventh year of release, or the year of release. Write that down.

“When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord.” He is telling us what to do when we enter the land, and we entered the land under Joshua, not under Moses. The year of release, and the jubilee, did not begin until we were in the land.

“In the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land” … “thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard. That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap.” You don’t go in and farm it. Whatever grows of itself during that seventh year is what you eat.

“The sabbath of the land shall be meat for you”: for thee, the servant, the maid, the hired servant, the stranger that sojourneth, the cattle and the beast. All the increase of that year is food for everyone, but nobody works the land. The seventh year of release is built on the seventh-day sabbath.

precepts.why:
Now you might ask, if we are not farming in the seventh year, what are we going to eat? The law asks the same question: “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase.” And the Lord answers: “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” The sixth year is going to grow enough to cover you for three years.

Think about that with the seventh-day sabbath. Brothers and sisters say, I got to work on the Sabbath because that’s my money day. Then you obviously don’t believe what we just read. God said work six days and rest on the Sabbath, and the question, I got to make my money, is the same question asked in verse 20. The Most High already answered it.

sense.text: “At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles.” The release came at the feast of tabernacles: that is when you released the land, the servants and the debt.

“At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.” Every creditor that lent to his neighbour or his brother “shall release it” … “because it is called the Lord’s release.” If you lend someone something, at the end of seven years that debt is taken care of. It is released.
“Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again: but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release.” The release is for your brother. The foreigner still pays.

“Only if thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God” … “thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt reign over many nations, but they shall not reign over thee.” That is the blessing if we keep the commandments: nations would not lend to us, we would not have to borrow, they would borrow from us. That did happen in the time of David and the time of Solomon.

“If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren”: one of thy brethren, a poor man. “Thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother: but thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need.”

“Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand.” Imagine it is the sixth year, and I lend you something you would have to pay back, but next year is the year of release, so I say, I ain’t giving you nothing, because it is only twelve more months and he won’t have to pay it back. If you do that and “he cry unto the Lord against thee” … “it be sin unto thee.” Give to him and don’t be grieved, because for this thing the Lord will bless all your works.

“For the poor shall never cease out of the land.” In verses 5 and 6 the Lord said that if we kept the commandments we would lend and not borrow. But here he says the poor will never cease out of the land. What was the Lord letting us know? We were not going to be keeping those commandments for long. So he commands, “Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.”

“If thy brother, an Hebrew man, or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee.” This is very important. Sold unto thee means they were poor and could not take care of themselves: they lacked food, water and shelter, so they sold themselves to you and worked for you. That is why the word is servant and not slave; we tend to get those words confused. They were only to serve six years.

“Thou shalt not let him go away empty: thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress.” Why? So that he or she can have a fresh start, and be self-sufficient on their own.

“And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.” That is what helps us understand the law that says love your neighbour as you love yourself: all those laws intertwine.

precepts.why:
Christ said the same thing Moses said: “For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.” The law already said “the poor shall never cease out of the land.”

The blessing of verses 5 and 6 was for keeping the commandments, with no poor among us and nations borrowing from us. That the poor would always be there was the Lord letting us know we would not keep his commandments for long. So the command stands: open your hand wide to your poor brother.

sense.text: Then there is the year of jubilee, which comes every fifty years, when all property and land returns to the tribe of the family. The word comes from the ram’s horn sounded to begin it, and it means release, liberty. “Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years” … “forty and nine years.” Doesn’t that sound like Pentecost? It is the same concept.
The trumpet of the jubilee sounds “on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement.” Jubilee begins on the Day of Atonement.

“Proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof” … “ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family.” If someone of the tribe of Benjamin lets me use his land to grow crops, by the fiftieth year I have to give it back. If someone of Judah kept it, that would mess up Benjamin’s inheritance. The land must stay inside the tribe. It ensured no citizen would remain poor or a slave forever, and the land belonged to the Lord, so no man was to pile it up for himself. Freedom was always the ultimate goal.

“Ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it.” It is very similar to the seventh year of release: don’t farm the land, don’t work it, let it go for that year. And in the jubilee “ye shall return every man unto his possession.” There is a spirit in the land; the Most High wanted us to see that there is a connection between the people and the land. Ezra shows it with the woman who came to him, who was Jerusalem.
“Ye shall not oppress one another.” Don’t oppress one another in buying and selling.

“According to the multitude of years thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price of it.” A person who sold land was really selling a number of crops. If the jubilee just ended and you get the land for close to fifty years, you will get a lot of crops, so the price is higher. If there is one year left before the jubilee, you cannot grow much, so the price is low.

“Ye shall not therefore oppress one another; but thou shalt fear thy God.” You ever see how black people today cheat each other and undercut each other? That is why we have to come back to the Bible and apply these basic principles; then our businesses will do okay. We always try to oppress one another, and then we get mad when our people go and do business with the Chinese man. Why are you going to the Chinese man, brother? Because look what you are trying to do to me. Like I’m paying your mortgage.
Do the statutes and keep the judgments, “and ye shall dwell in the land in safety. And the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill.” You will always have enough.

“What shall we eat the seventh year?” No farming, no crops. “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” That is for everyone who says, I have to break the Sabbath because I have to make my money. It is connected to the seventh-day Sabbath, where we bake what we will bake and lay it up for the seventh: the Most High increases the sixth day, and here he increases the sixth year. It is all spiritual. “Until her fruits come in ye shall eat of the old store”: what you had gathered.
“The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine.” The land belongs to the Lord.

“If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.” A family member could come and redeem what he had to sell because he was poor.

If he has none to redeem it and later is able himself, he counts the years and restores “the overplus”, the extra, to the man he sold it to. If he cannot, the land stays in the hand of the buyer “until the year of jubile: and in the jubile it shall go out, and he shall return unto his possession.” Whether you had the money or not, it comes back to you in the fiftieth year.

A dwelling house in a walled city can be redeemed within a full year; after that it is established for ever to him that bought it, “it shall not go out in the jubile.” That was the exception. But the houses of the villages without walls “shall go out in the jubile”: they go back to the owner.

“The cities of the Levites” … “may the Levites redeem at any time.” The Levites lived in the suburbs of Israel. Levi was scattered among all the tribes, all through Israel, and the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold, “for it is their perpetual possession.”

“If thy brother be waxen poor” … “then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner.” Pay close attention. Stranger here does not mean another race of people. It means one Israelite in the land of another tribe: a man of Judah in the land of Simeon is a stranger there.
“Take thou no usury of him, or increase.” Usury means interest. I give you a hundred dollars, you have to give me back two hundred: don’t do that. Nor lend him victuals for increase.

“Thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: but as an hired servant.” A bondservant is like chattel slavery, and your brother is not to be made that. What we call a job today, back then they called you a servant. He is poor, he needs help, so I employ him, and he serves “unto the year of jubile.”

Then he departs with his children and returns to his family and the possession of his fathers, “For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.”

“Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour.” Rigour is hardship: busting him in the head, whooping him. You don’t rule over your brother like that. That is the difference between the servant of the law and chattel slavery. Christianity, especially in the time of chattel slavery, took the words of the Bible, servants, obey your masters, and had you thinking of being rigorously destroyed in chattel slavery. That is not what this is. The Bible clearly makes a difference between how we deal with our own citizens and how we deal with hardcore slaves, which are the nations.

“Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you.” Your bondmen and bondmaids shall be of the other nations. And “of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy” … “and they shall be your possession.” Now the word stranger is talking about the heathen, as the verse above explains.

“They shall be your bondmen for ever.” The other nations were not released in the jubilee; they remained our slaves, passed down as an inheritance from generation to generation. “But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” There is the distinction.

If a sojourner or stranger waxes rich and thy brother waxes poor and sells himself to him: this is not saying we sold ourselves to other nations. It is another tribe. I am poor in the land of Judah, my land is jacked up, and I go work for a man of Gad. Esau will use this chapter and try to cause confusion with the word stranger, saying, see, the other nations. No, that is about Israel. One of his brethren, his uncle, his uncle’s son, any nigh of kin, may redeem him, “or if he be able, he may redeem himself”: he might come into some money while he is working.

The price of his redemption is “according unto the number of years” left from now to the jubilee. It is the same concept as the land: many years left, the price is higher; few years left, the price is lower.

“The other shall not rule with rigour over him in thy sight”, which goes back to verse 43. And if he is not redeemed, “he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he, and his children with him”, which goes back to verse 41.

“For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.” This tells you plainly the Israelites are God’s servants. Everybody on the planet is not God’s servants. You can’t make this stuff up.

precepts.why:
Here is an example of how the word stranger is used among Israel: the censers were “a memorial unto the children of Israel, that no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before the Lord; that he be not as Korah.” That stranger means Judah, Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Gad, Reuben and so forth.

If you are not of the seed of Aaron, you are a stranger. So when Leviticus 25 says “though he be a stranger, or a sojourner”, it is speaking of an Israelite of another tribe, not another race of people.

sense.text: If a man sanctifies his field from the year of jubilee it stands at the estimation; if after the jubilee, the priest reckons “the money according to the years that remain, even unto the year of the jubile.” The same count of years to the jubilee sets the value.

If he that sanctified the field will redeem it, “he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it.” You want to redeem your land early, you add the fifth part. The fifth part is an extra twenty percent: if the field is valued at a hundred dollars, a fifth is twenty, and you pay a hundred and twenty.

“If he will not redeem the field, or if he have sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more” and in the jubilee it is “holy unto the Lord” … “the possession thereof shall be the priest’s.” The priest owns it. People vowed part of their fields to the Lord and then sold them to escape their vows; they try to be slick, so the Most High said, I got something for them: they could never get their land back.

If a man sanctifies a field he bought, which is not of his own possession, that’s not his property. “In the year of the jubile the field shall return unto him of whom it was bought, even to him to whom the possession of the land did belong.” It goes back to that tribe.

The chief fathers of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh: this is the tribe of Manasseh. The Lord had commanded that the inheritance of Zelophehad be given “unto his daughters”, because he had no sons. This is for the brothers that only have daughters.

“If they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes” … “then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers.” The inheritance would go to her husband. If she is Manasseh and marries Judah, now Judah owns land that is not supposed to be Judah’s. And the jubilee would not cancel that out: it would not go back to Manasseh, it would stay with Judah, because she married Judah.

“Only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.” That is the law right there. If you have all daughters and you have land and property, they have to marry within the tribe, so that another tribe of Israel does not take possession of it for ever. Brothers with all sons are looking for a brother with all daughters; see how it works.

“So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” Every daughter that possesses an inheritance “shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father.” Judah married outside the tribe of Judah and Ephraim outside of Ephraim, but there was a special clause when it came to property and land: the woman was not allowed to do that.

precepts.why:
That is what Tobit was making reference to: “take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Our fathers from the beginning “married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.” Shall inherit the land: the marriage within the tribe and the land go together.

“Love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble.” It is pride when you don’t want to marry a woman of your own race, your own tribe. Anytime people say love is love: God said love thy brethren and despise them not, and despising your own people ain’t what God said. “And in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.” You will lose everything.

You see it all in the news. Halle Berry has to pay child support to both her exes, and every time she paid her Edomite husband he said, Thank you, nigger. He wanted their daughter’s hair lightened and straightened: I want my children to look white. Serena Williams married out after all her father went through for her, and he did not even come to the wedding. Shannon Sharpe lost millions over a young white girl from the gym. Lewdness is the mother of famine. The Bible is a true book.

sense.text: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” The seventh year of release was a year when debts between Israelites were forgiven and the land rested; the jubilee did all that and also restored the land to its families. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if married, his wife goes out with him.

“If his master have given him a wife” … “the wife and her children shall be her master’s.” What we call a boss today is the word master. You work for me, I give you one of my daughters as a wife, and if you have children with her, they stay with me.

If the servant says “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”, his master brings him to the judges and to the door post and bores “his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.” An awl is a tool like a spike, put through the earlobe.

“If a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.” Like in the South back in the day, when you were up in age your daughters went out and got work for people. There is a difference between her and the menservants.

If her master betrothed her to himself and she pleases him not, he must let her be redeemed: “to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.” It is against God’s law to sell her to a strange nation; he dealt deceitfully, because he didn’t marry her.
If he takes another wife, “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.” And if he does not provide those three, “then shall she go out free without money.”
“He shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That’s the law. You steal one ox, you pay back five; one sheep, you pay back four.

“If a thief be found breaking up”: breaking and entering, breaking into somebody’s house. If he is smitten that he die, “there shall no blood be shed for him.” This is night time. You don’t know what he has in his hands, it is dark, your life is in danger, and you put him to death; there is no sacrifice for that.

“If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him.” Now it is day time. And “if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” He was supposed to pay back four sheep and has nothing, so now he has to work for you. You would be mad with somebody like that and give him the most grievous chores. You own him.
If the theft is found alive in his hand, “he shall restore double.”

If a man puts his beast in another man’s field or vineyard to eat it up, “of the best of his own field” … “shall he make restitution.” You don’t bring your animals into my yard to eat up my vegetables. That’s black people.
“He that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.” Down south they shoot firecrackers and set a field on fire. The Bible says you pay restitution, even if he’s only twelve.

If a man delivers his neighbour money or stuff to keep and it is stolen, if the thief is found “let him pay double.” If not, the master of the house goes before the judges “to see whether he have put his hand unto his neighbour’s goods”: to see if you are a liar. You know how black people do: It wasn’t me, somebody stole it, and he helps you look for it with it in his back pocket. You can tell it is black folks we are reading about here. These laws were written for us.
Every manner of trespass comes “before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double.” We had courts of law.

If a beast left in keeping dies, is hurt or is “driven away”, which means it ran away, “no man seeing it”, an oath of the Lord is between them both. But if it is stolen from him, he makes restitution to the owner.

If it is torn in pieces he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrows and it is hurt or dies, the owner not being with it, “he shall surely make it good.” These are what we call negro proof laws: they had to be written so that we would not do evil to each other, and this is exactly why we are getting jacked up now.

This is what the Lord told us in advance about the land: “That your days may be multiplied” … “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” For us, heaven has always been upon the earth. When we enter the land it shall be as the days of heaven upon the earth. And the jubilee did not start until we got into the land.

If we keep the commandments, the Lord will “drive out all these nations from before you”, because the Canaanites filled the land, “and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.” Possess means own. We shall own these nations.

“Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours.” Every place your feet touch is your land: that is heaven on earth. And it gives the borders: “from the wilderness”, the wilderness of Egypt on the other side of the Nile, “and Lebanon”, Lebanon was ours, “from the river, the river Euphrates”, which runs up through Syria, “even unto the uttermost sea”, the Mediterranean. So when people say Congo or Kenya is the real Israel, what are they talking about? It gives you the layout of the land right here.

precepts.why:
Genesis 15 goes with Deuteronomy 11:21-24: “Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates.” The river of Egypt is the Nile.

The same thing God told Abraham is what we took. We were fighting for it from the time of Joshua, and from David and Solomon we fully had it all.

sense.text: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob”: not on everybody, only on Jacob. “And will yet choose Israel”: we might be at the bottom of society, but he will yet choose us. “And set them in their own land”: God sets us in the land, not the League of Nations or the United Nations. “And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.”

“And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place.” All the nations go back to the land God originally gave them. The Arabs took all of North Africa: Egypt, Libya, Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco, Mauritania, northern Sudan, Yemen, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Iraq, Syria. That is stolen land. Egypt was Mizraim, and Put was up there too, and the Hamites scattered among the Israelites are going right back there. “And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids” … “and they shall rule over their oppressors.” That is what we read in Leviticus 25.
“In the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.”

precepts.why:
Why does Isaiah say “the strangers shall be joined”? Because of what we read in Leviticus 25: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you.” And “of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy” … “they shall be your bondmen for ever.”

That law cannot be in effect now, because right now we are the slaves; we are in a foreign land. But when we get back to the land, these laws go back into full effect. That is why Isaiah 14 says the strangers shall be joined and cleave to the house of Jacob, and Israel shall possess them “for servants and handmaids.”

sense.text: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired. God is instructing the twelve tribes to gather ourselves together. Wake up.

“Before the decree bring forth”: the decree is the destruction that is prophesied to come, “before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you.” Get yourselves together before destruction comes. Things are moving at a quicker pace: President Trump is forcing prophecies to come to pass and forcing the Israelites to do what the Bible says.

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment.” Meek means humble to God’s word, and wrought his judgment means done his laws. In case you are confused about who gathers together, verse 3 tells you: the men and women who want to do God’s commandments without making excuses. “It may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” That is what you want. We can only be with those who are meek to God’s laws. There is a camp that says if you wear fringes they will throw you out; they will wear a suit and tie but not a fringe with a border of blue. We can’t gather with people like that.

“For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up.” Gaza is going to be destroyed, and it even gives the time: Ashdod at noon day. Ekron is right up near Jerusalem.

“Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the Cherethites!” That is the Palestinians. The Philistines aren’t there anymore; the Palestinians are, and that is who “the land of the Philistines” is making reference to. “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.” They are not getting pushed out of the land; God said he will destroy them.

“The sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds”: the coast of the Mediterranean, where Gaza is. “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: in the houses of Ashkelon shall they lie down.” Judah is going to live on the sea coast, in the houses of Ashkelon that got wiped out, “for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.”

precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” Some morons say, let’s go join ourselves with the camp that believes John the Baptist was a wicked nigger. You can’t join with that. Or with the camp that believes men don’t have to work, get seven or eight women and let them work for you. We can’t join with that.

So when Zephaniah says gather yourselves together, it is not every camp that calls itself Israel. People ask, why aren’t y’all all together? Because two cannot walk together except they be agreed.

Judah is going to live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” The coast of Zephaniah 2:7 is for the remnant of Judah, and God builds the cities of Judah for us to dwell in and own.

sense.text: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.” That is the twelve tribes. “And I will build it as in the days of old.”

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jews today. The word Jew comes from Judah, which means praise of Yahawah, and those people are not the praise of Yahawah. And there are people calling themselves Christians, which means the anointed ones, and they are not the anointed ones.

“I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities.” He is going to bring us back to the land. There are waste cities all over there now, and after Armageddon there will be more waste, and we are going to build. Actually, we ain’t lifting a damn thing. We are going to have slaves, and they will build the things for us.
“I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land.”

“I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” Write it down: Carmel was Judah’s, and Bashan was Manasseh’s. Things are going to get switched around when we go back.

“The iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He is going to wipe away our iniquity. That is what it means that he will yet choose Israel.

precepts.why: “The uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward.” Read on to verse 55 and Carmel is among the cities of Judah. Carmel belonged to Judah.
“Maon, Carmel, and Ziph”: Carmel is in the lot of the tribe of Judah. So when Jeremiah says Israel shall feed on Carmel, that was Judah’s land.

“Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh” … “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan.” Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

So Jeremiah 50:19 has Israel feeding on Carmel and Bashan, Judah’s land and Manasseh’s land, and on mount Ephraim and Gilead. When we go back, things are going to get switched around.

sense.text: This shows how things get switched around. “They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau”: where Edom used to dwell, we are going to take that whole area. “And they of the plain the Philistines”: we are going to take Palestine. “And they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.”

“The captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites”, the land of Israel, “even unto Zarephath”, which is Lebanon. “And the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad”, which is the region of Asia Minor and Spain, “shall possess the cities of the south.”
“And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom, “and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.”

precepts.why:
“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon.” He is going to bring us out of captivity into Gilead, which is Obadiah 19, and into Lebanon, which is the Zarephath of Obadiah 20.

“And place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us when we go back to the land. Keep that in mind: that is why Obadiah has Israel possessing even unto Zarephath, which is Lebanon.

sense.text: “The land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”: there will be too many of us. “And they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: the ones we lost are the two thirds, the wicked Israelites. The rest “shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said, in my Father’s house are many mansions.

precepts.why:
In case somebody asks what “lost the other” means: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” All the land is Babylon, which is America. Two out of every three Israelites here shall die.

“And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined” … “I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” The third part is the children Isaiah speaks of, who say the place is too strait for them.

sense.text: People like to say the Israelites stole the Canaanites’ land. We didn’t steal nothing; the land was ours, and anything a slave owns is yours. Here is the prophecy, from Noah: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.”

“Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.” Israel comes out of Shem. The Canaanites shall be the servants of Israel. At this time there were no twelve tribes yet; Israel did not come until Jacob’s name was changed. So Noah speaks of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
“God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem.” Whose tents would Japheth be living in? Shem’s, the Israelites’. Everything belongs to Shem. “And Canaan shall be his servant.”

precepts.why:
Here is the precept, in case that is too hard: “Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes.”

God made the world for our sake. That is why Canaan is Shem’s servant and Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem: the earth and the people in it were made for the chosen people.

sense.text: Here is the next prophecy. “The kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven”: what is under the whole heaven is the planet earth. It “shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” Everything is going back to the Israelites, everything on this planet, including the planet. “Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him”: everybody is going to obey Christ.
“Hitherto is the end of the matter.” That is the whole plan of God. “My cogitations much troubled me”: his thoughts much troubled him, “but I kept the matter in my heart.”

precepts.why:
Who are the saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” Even means indeed: indeed the children of Israel.

So the Israelites are the saints, and when Daniel says the kingdom under the whole heaven shall be given to “the people of the saints of the most High”, it is given to Israel.

This goes along with the other scriptures. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The context of the chapter is Israel going off, and because Israel went off, everything went out of whack.

“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” This goes with what we read in Esdras and in Daniel: the whole planet earth belongs to the Israelites. We are not the Most High, but we are the powers on this earth, the judges of the whole planet.

And verse 5 shows it was always meant to be that way: “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” If the Israelites are not ruling the planet, it is in gross darkness, and all the foundations are out of the natural way God made them. When we are ruling with God’s commandments and laws, everything will be in line.

sense.text: What happened as a result of us disobeying the year of release and the jubilee? King Zedekiah made a covenant with all the people at Jerusalem “to proclaim liberty unto them; that every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free” … “to wit, of a Jew his brother.” If Israelites worked for you, you had to follow the year of release and the jubilee. It is not talking about the other nations; it is about the Hebrews, our people.

They obeyed and let them go. “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection.” Do you see what we did? This is some negro stuff right here.

“At the end of seven years let ye go every man his brother an Hebrew” … “when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free from thee.” That is the year of release, the covenant made when he brought us out of Egypt. “But your fathers hearkened not unto me.”

They had turned and done right, proclaiming liberty in the house called by his name, “But ye turned and polluted my name”, and brought those they had set at liberty back into subjection. We can’t get right.

“Ye have not hearkened unto me, in proclaiming liberty” … “behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, saith the Lord, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” God’s liberty is to get rid of you from him. That is Deuteronomy 28 right there.

The princes, the eunuchs, the priests and all who passed between the parts of the calf, he gives into the hand of their enemies, and their dead bodies are meat for the fowls and the beasts. We wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude to us: the elites among us, those who had money, did that to the ones who didn’t, and the Most High got mad.

Zedekiah and his princes go into the hand of “the king of Babylon’s army, which are gone up from you. Behold, I will command, saith the Lord, and cause them to return to this city” … “and burn it with fire.” Babylon had just left, and God said, I am going to have Babylon come right back because of what you did. That is the result of us hating our brothers, not loving our neighbour as we love ourselves.
“There was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.” This is about the debts we owed one another.

“We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth”: there was a famine. Others borrowed money for the king’s tribute upon their lands and vineyards. These are the lands and vineyards we were reading about all class.

“Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children”: we are one people, the same. “And, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants” … “neither is it in our power to redeem them.” The elites of Israel were putting the poor Israelites in bondage to them, like the talented tenth, the little groups black people like to set up. And the poor had no money to redeem them, “for other men have our lands and vineyards.”

Nehemiah was very angry, because we had just come out of captivity in Persia and this was going on among us. He consulted with himself and “rebuked the nobles, and the rulers”: the nobles are the elites of Israel, the wealthy. “Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.” Nehemiah got all Israel to turn against them: imagine a million negroes against maybe five hundred. You are going to do what I say. Verses 6 and 7 are close to what this country set up in the Declaration of Independence: if the government turns rogue, it is up to the people to abolish that government. Listen, nobles, if you deal with us wrong, we are going to put hands on you.

“We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren?” Now you are doing the same thing the other nations did to us. “Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.”

“Ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies?” … “let us leave off this usury. Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards”: this day, not tomorrow, and “the hundredth part of the money.” Give it back.
“We will restore them, and will require nothing of them.” You see what fear can do. Fear is a game changer; that is what the great assembly was.

“So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise.” His labour is his lands. Notice the threat: if any of you nobles go back on your word, we take everything from you. That is gangster, in righteousness; sometimes that is how you have to roll. Nobody is teaching Israel laws like this, and our people desperately need them; stop wasting time debating Christians and teach the people the law of God so they can get better.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek captivity. What did the Greeks do? “The merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves.” This slavery is different from what we read in Leviticus 25. We look at the slave auctions and think this is the first time it ever happened; no, the Greeks did this too. “A power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them”: the other nations were helping the Greeks.

precepts.why:
What kind of slavery is 1 Maccabees 3:41? This kind: “Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery, the curse.

It is not the hired servant of Leviticus 25 who serves his brother to the jubilee. It is the captivity of the curse, Israel sold to the nations.

sense.text: “But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy.” Jason was an Israelite. We think our people love themselves; no, Jason hated his own people. He treated them as “his enemies, and not his countrymen”, because he wanted to please the Greeks. Don’t be surprised when you see black men and black women do all they can to please the enemies of our race. They will be worse on you than white men.

“He obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites.” He was a treasonous negro. The Most High does not like traitors; he can’t stand that thing.

He fled “from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen.” Forsaker of God’s laws, an open enemy of the Israelites, and he was cast out into Egypt. Imagine being banished, not able to come back to your own country because you were a traitor.

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land.” He was doing it to his own people, and then it happened to him. He thought he would find succour among the Lacedemonians, where Sparta was. “And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all.” What goes around comes around.

When the king heard of it he thought Judea had revolted and took the city by force: “killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants.” This is what the Greeks were doing. Fourscore thousand destroyed in three days, eighty thousand, “and no fewer sold than slain”: sold as slaves.

precepts.why:
“But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.” Negroes do evil and think there won’t be a big payback. You are going to get it.

Jason drove many out of their country and perished in a strange land; he cast out many unburied and had none to mourn him. He received for the wrong he had done.

“He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius” … “commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort.” These scriptures show the Greeks selling us as slaves.

The best age is the movers and shakers that make a nation thrive, twenty-five to thirty-five or so. When you take the greatest, those of the best age, and leave the old and feeble, you destroy the nation. The colonialists did the same: they took the greatest of us.

sense.text: Rome got its foothold in our land before 70 AD: Pompey captured Jerusalem before Christ, left puppet rulers in place, and made Judea a Roman province, with taxes and military governors. Remember the Jews coming from all over: that is where the Israelites were coming from, “Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia.” You would ask why Judea is listed, since Judea is in the land of Israel. Because Judea was a Roman province.

Under Rome everything seemed somewhat stable, as you read in Matthew, while the factions fought for rule. “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” If we don’t do something, Rome is going to come in. Right now it is stable, the Romans gave us our positions and our authority, and we can’t let this Christ mess things up. That was the issue.

precepts.why:
They wanted Paul and could not get him, so “they drew Alexander out of the multitude”, and “when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.” Woman worship, feminism.

The townclerk, an associate of Paul who turned on him, appeased the people: “ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.” If Demetrius has a matter, “the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another”: let them go to court, “in a lawful assembly.”

“For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar.” In danger of what? Rome. Everything was stable, and there could be no uproars, or Rome would come in with its legions and decimate everybody. America lets black people march through the streets and burn things down; Rome didn’t play that. So he “dismissed the assembly.” Israel tried not to involve Rome except in life and death situations, and through that time of stability Israel was still trying to follow the laws of selling yourself to work when you were poor or owed a debt.

sense.text: These are the scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and dumb black people use to reject the Bible. “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ.” This is what we read at the beginning of the class in Leviticus 25 and Exodus. It ain’t talking about chattel slavery. Servants obey your masters, see, the Bible is evil, they say. No.

precepts.why:
In case you forgot: “if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile.” This is what the Apostle Paul was dealing with in the New Testament.

Then he returns to his family, “For they are my servants” … “they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour.” Rigour is chattel slavery. The servant Paul tells to obey his master is the Hebrew servant of the law.

“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God.” The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants. These were hired servants.

“If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” Notice: “If his master have given him a wife.” That is what “servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about; we are reading it here in Exodus.

And “if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free.” Why would he say I love my master? Because the brother treats him real good. Then his ear is bored through with an aul “and he shall serve him for ever.” That is not chattel slavery.

sense.text: “Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear.” This was in the slave Bible; Esau used it. “Not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” Some masters weren’t that nice. The law told them not to deal with Israel with rigour, but some were hard. The froward ones are the ones that don’t really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.” “For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

precepts.why:
This is what Esau did: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

They took this Bible and perverted it, making Peter’s words about servants into a command for chattel slavery.

Remember the thief: “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” He has to work for you.

How mad would you be with the man who broke into your house? You really wouldn’t like him much, and you have to see him every morning. That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me. Now I’m nigging and broke into your house, stealing your stuff, and you catch me, and now I got to work for you. He ain’t going to like me too much. That is who the froward master is, and why the servant who was “buffeted for your faults” is to take it patiently.

sense.text: “Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again.” Esau perverted this. Not answering again means not talking back.

“Not purloining.” Purloin means to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what we just read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with the brothers who were stealing and got caught and had to work it off. “But shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.”
“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Paul met him when he was under arrest.

“Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels.” Paul is writing to Philemon: receive him as if you were receiving me.

“Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel.” Paul could have kept him to help him with the gospel, but sent him back: “without thy mind would I do nothing”, so that if he stays, it is sent willingly, not of necessity.

“For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever.” He ran away from Philemon. Onesimus was a servant to Philemon. “Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”: deal with him as a brother.

“If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself. If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account.” Was he a servant because he was poor, or did he do something bad? He owed him: he stole something or broke something. Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites.

Now it jumps to chattel slavery. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations.” Those of us who remained in the land fell by Rome’s sword; Rome got tired of the Israelites, destroyed us, and enslaved the ones it didn’t kill. “And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Who is living in the land? Gentiles, until their rulership is finished, until Christ returns. Then came the empires: Rome set back up, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain, and the United States from 1776 until today. These were the times of chattel slavery; all these empires had us in it.

“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” He tells us to fear not. “When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee”: no matter what we go through, God is with us. “When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned”: that is protection.

“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” In order to deliver us out of captivity, God had to destroy the Egyptian army; Ethiopia was a help to them and he destroyed them too; and Seba, which is Somalia.

“Since thou wast precious in my sight”: we are the apple of his eye. “I have loved thee”: that is God so loved the world. “Therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to kill people; I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

“I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”: that is us here in the western hemisphere. “I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” You think they are just going to give God’s people back? No. Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us, and he will destroy those nations.
“Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him.”

precepts.why:
“But we thy people (whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover) are given into their hands.”

That is what “precious in my sight” means: we are his fervent lover. We are his bride, his wife.

God won’t just ask for his people back. “And in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” “His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” What are people arguing about the name for?

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses.” There are armies in heaven. Christ is coming back with armies to deliver the Israelites from the north and the south and the ends of the earth.

The Christians want their white Jesus to come back throwing flowers. John Hagee, that big fat Edomite in Texas, said Christ is going to set his government up and get the Democrats and the Republicans in order, and the people went crazy clapping. But “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous; we have to accept the destruction of the enemies too. That is what Isaiah 43 says: men given for us.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punished our adversaries, he glorified us. We are the bride of Christ; Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

“It shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north”: that is North America, “and from all the lands whither he had driven them”: the Caribbean, Africa, all the lands we are scattered in. “And I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

“Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” The creature is you and me.

It is talking about us being delivered, not only from this body, but from captivity, into liberty. He that redeemed us brings us out.

sense.text: “Come near, ye nations, to hear” … “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies.” This is the decree we read about in Zephaniah 2: before the decree bring forth, gather yourselves together. How many nations? All nations. “He hath utterly destroyed them”: Isaiah writes it in the past tense because he saw it; he witnessed it.
“Their stink shall come up out of their carcases”: their dead bodies, “and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.”

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: bombs going off, that mushroom effect. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: their helicopters, jets, planes, satellites, missiles. America is so confident its technology will always work, but on that day the angels only have to snap their fingers and it all falls out of the sky.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. The Jehovah’s Witnesses like to go around and say they were destroyed already and are no more. Then who is Christ coming in on? That is destruction right there.

“The Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek”: good tidings means gospel. “To bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.” Where are the captives? How can you read captive and think it is everybody? “And the opening of the prison to them that are bound.” We are bound in the prison we call America, in the Caribbean, in whatever lands we are in.

“To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to proclaim and deliver his people. “To comfort all that mourn”: why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion”: Zion is another name for the Israelites. “Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning” … “that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord.” All we have to do in this truth is endure to the end.
“They shall build the old wastes” … “and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.” That is what we read in Amos 9.

“And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.” We won’t have to feed our own flocks. That is Isaiah 14:1-2 and Leviticus 25 from verse 45 down: all the laws of the strangers being in our service for ever are coming back into full effect. The sons of the alien are the other nations. You got the nerve to call Mexicans illegal aliens. No, cracker, you’re the illegal alien.

“But ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves.” They talk about black people always bragging; you haven’t seen bragging until you get to this day.

“For your shame ye shall have double”: for the shame we have received in this country and all the world, we shall have double. “Therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.”

“For I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering.” Don’t give a sheep you stole as an offering to the Lord; God said I hate that thing. “I will make an everlasting covenant with them.”

“And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people.” Our children shall be known among all nations. No matter where we go on this planet, they will know our children by name and move out of their way. “All that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” Today you want to talk to your boss and they turn their back on you. On that day they are going to beg for your attention.

precepts.why:
Here is a precept to it: “Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee”: all the nations that afflict us. “And I will save her that halteth”: we are the ones that halt, because we are captive. “And gather her that was driven out.”

“And I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.” We get that fame and that glory, and our children get it too; everybody is going to acknowledge who we are. “For I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes.” That is the seed which the Lord hath blessed, known among the Gentiles.

sense.text: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” This is the Lord, Christ, the son of God. “This that is glorious in his apparel”: it ain’t a sheet or a robe; when you see Christ’s garment you will say that’s bad to the bone. “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save”: that is Christ speaking to us.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” This is Isaiah saying to Christ, why are you red, what is all that on your clothes? It looks like you were stomping grapes.

“I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod the nations and killed them alone; he did not need the help of the twelve tribes. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” That is what the wine represents: their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. That is the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of vengeance of Isaiah 61. Black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks; could you imagine Jacob and Esau sitting in the same church and this being read?

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” Who are the poor? The poor of Zion; you don’t even have to go to Isaiah 14, because Isaiah 61:1-3 tells you it is them that mourn in Zion. “He hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives”: we are the captives. You ain’t talking about everybody; remember Rome was dominating Israel at this time. “And recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind. “To set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee. We better accept that. Could you imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors sitting side by side? It makes no damn sense. The gospel of Jesus, we are the same, we equal: shut the hell up, slave.

precepts.why:
“What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That tells you who the poor are: the poor of his people, the poor of Zion. The gospel to the poor is the gospel to captive Israel.

sense.text: “This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance.” Remember this: “the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles.”

“There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.” We are seeing scoffers in these last days like never before. Every black urban apologist is a scoffer: they don’t believe the Bible, they don’t believe Christ is black, they think Jesus is Cesare Borgia and the white man is coming to deliver them.

“Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” They say everything has continued from our fathers and our fathers’ fathers; nothing has changed.

“For this they willingly are ignorant of.” We can take them to Deuteronomy and show how things were prophesied and have come to fruition, and it fits us perfect to a T. How can you say the Bible ain’t a true book? “By the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.” That is the flood: God killed everybody on the planet except Noah, his three sons and their wives.
“But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” This earth is reserved unto fire.

Why did Peter say “one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day”? Because of the scoffers of verse 4. Don’t get mixed up with time. Generations go by with us, but with the Lord it is only a day.

“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”, saying God ain’t going to do nothing, he don’t see us. “But is longsuffering to us-ward”: the us-ward is the beloved of verse 1. “Not willing that any should perish”: he doesn’t want Israel to perish, “but that all should come to repentance”: the elect, that is who will come to repentance.

“The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise”: destruction. “And the elements shall melt with fervent heat”: the hottest heat, nuclear heat. “The earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.” All we take pride in here in America shall be burnt up, so don’t get too attached.

“What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness.” We have to act right and speak right. A lot of our conversation is filth and sports; we have to train ourselves to speak the words of this book. Godliness is our actions, our works, and the way we live must be the way we speak.

“Wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.” The heavens are the nations that dwell in their heaven, the world superpowers, and the elements within them shall be dissolved and burnt up.

“Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” Esau ain’t going to be there enjoying nothing. Righteousness dwells there because our people shall be all righteous.

“Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.” Without spot means without sin. Be blameless, brothers and sisters.

precepts.why:
Who is the beloved of the Lord? “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

All the way of knowledge is the Bible. The Bible does not belong to all nations on earth; it was given only to the beloved, the Israelites. So Peter’s “beloved” is Israel, and the “us-ward” of verse 9 is the beloved.

Holy conversation: they used to say of one brother that if you weren’t talking about the Bible, don’t talk to him; he wanted to hear nothing but the scripture. Paul said the same: “For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”

He trained himself. All I want to hear is the Bible. I don’t want to hear Betty got a big booty, how many touchdowns somebody ran, or how far he did the jump shot. I don’t want to hear that crap. That is all holy conversation: we have to train our minds and our spirits to learn it.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders.” That means the white man is going to be subdued, because he is the violent man behind every coup and every war. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day” … “but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.” The sun and moon are not done away with; they will be there, but the Israelites won’t need them, because the Lord will be our light. “Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself”: our understanding shall no more go down or withdraw itself. “And the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

This is what was wanted: “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever.” For ever. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: a whole lot of children. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” That is the new earth “wherein dwelleth righteousness”: righteousness dwells there because our people shall be all righteous.
